themes_detail.label: Abandoned Bikes Surge
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned bike complaints spiked to 4 reports THIS WEEK compared to a 0.5-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 700% increase—suggesting either a new dumping problem or enforcement gap in Midwood/Ocean Parkway.
evidence: 4 abandoned bike complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 average weekly baseline over prior 8 weeks (700% spike)
Z-score of 4.95 indicates statistically significant anomaly
No prior pattern of bike abandonment complaints in this district suggests new or emerging issue
reporting_angles: Are bike-share programs or rental services dumping inventory in the neighborhood?
Interview Parks Dept and Sanitation about enforcement protocols for abandoned bikes and timeline for removal

themes_detail.label: Sewer & Sidewalk Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Root/sewer/sidewalk condition complaints jumped to 7 reports LAST WEEK, up 273% from the 1.9-complaint weekly average—a potential indicator of aging infrastructure failure or recent weather damage affecting multiple blocks.
evidence: 7 complaints filed last week vs. 1.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (273% spike, z-score 4.04)
Suggests cluster of related infrastructure failures across the district rather than isolated incidents
High human impact: sidewalk hazards and sewer backups directly affect resident safety and property
reporting_angles: Map complaint locations to identify whether failures cluster on specific blocks or infrastructure age patterns
Interview DEP about known sewer issues, recent weather events, and maintenance backlog in CD 314

themes_detail.label: Air Quality Concerns Emerge
themes_detail.summary: Air quality complaints reached 4 reports 2 WEEKS AGO, a 433% jump from the 0.8-complaint weekly average—an unusual spike for this district that warrants investigation into industrial activity, construction dust, or vehicle emissions sources.
evidence: 4 air quality complaints filed 2 weeks ago vs. 0.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (433% spike, z-score 3.92)
First notable air quality complaint cluster in available data for this district
Coincides with active construction permits (351 filed in last 90 days, including 10 full demolitions)
reporting_angles: Cross-reference air quality complaints with active DOB demolition and alteration permits to identify dust sources
Speak with residents about odors, dust, or respiratory symptoms; check if complaints cluster near construction sites or truck routes

themes_detail.label: Safety Complaints Double
themes_detail.summary: Safety-related 311 complaints reached 15 reports 2 WEEKS AGO, up 103% from the 7.4-complaint weekly average—the broadest spike among emerging issues—indicating either a crime cluster, street hazard event, or perception shift in the community.
evidence: 15 safety complaints filed 2 weeks ago vs. 7.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (103% spike, z-score 3.33)
Largest absolute complaint spike among emerging issues, suggesting broader resident concern
311 category is broad; need reporting to determine whether spike reflects crime, infrastructure hazards, or perception/reporting change
reporting_angles: Request NYPD crime data for CD 314 over past 2-3 weeks to determine if safety spike correlates with actual crime incidents
Conduct community interviews and social media scan to understand what residents perceive as unsafe (street conditions, crime, traffic, construction hazards)

themes_detail.label: Appliance/Electrical Infrastructure Stress
themes_detail.summary: Appliance complaints spiked to 29 reports 2 WEEKS AGO (161% above the 11.1-complaint average), and electrical complaints hit 3 reports 3 WEEKS AGO (700% above the 0.4-complaint average)—together suggesting potential power supply issues or aging electrical systems affecting multiple buildings.
evidence: Appliance complaints: 29 filed 2 weeks ago vs. 11.1 weekly average (161% spike, z-score 4.12)
Electrical complaints: 3 filed 3 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly average (700% spike, z-score 5.42)
Convergence of two infrastructure categories suggests systemic power or electrical issue rather than isolated failures
reporting_angles: Interview Con Edison about power outages, voltage fluctuations, or infrastructure work in the district over the past 3-4 weeks
Identify geographic cluster of complaints; cross-check with utility work maps and building ages to assess electrical system vulnerability
